name: Lima
comment: Every pattern is RE2 syntax: no lookaround, backreference, atomic group or possessive quantifier (editors/shared/grammar-fragments.ts). Patterns marked GENERATED are written by editors/shared/scripts/generate-grammar-fragments.ts.

comment.comment: Lima Core 1.3 §4, §8: outside quotes, a # begins a comment at the start of a line or after whitespace; any other #, \# too, is text. The whitespace before it is matched outside the comment's scope. GENERATED:textmate-comment

line-continuation.comment: Lima Core §6.1.6: inside a `|` block, a line beginning with `^^` continues the previous line.

mapping-key.comment: An entry, after an object item's dash too: an unquoted, single-quoted or double-quoted key, and a colon followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line (Core 1.3 §5.1). The rule consumes the separator's whitespace, so it also matches what may start the value there: `|` alone, a literal block scalar (§6.1.5), or a comment, which leaves the key bare (§4). A double-quoted key's backslash escapes (Core §5.2) keep an escaped quote from closing it early. GENERATED:textmate-mapping-key

array-dash.comment: Block sequence item marker: `-` at the start of a line, alone or followed by whitespace (Core 1.3 §7.2), and what may start the item's value: `|` alone or a comment. `>` folded scalars are not supported. GENERATED:textmate-array-dash

value.comment: Scalars match where the scan stands; a date comes before plain words and plain words before the other scalars, so that these match whole words only.

reference-document.comment: Lima References 2.1 §2.1: ${document.path} reads a value from the current document. Inactive (literal) inside quoted strings. GENERATED:textmate-document-reference
reference-document.name: variable.other.reference.document.lima

reference-partial.comment: Lima References 2.1 §2.2: $(partial.path) reads from the partials option. GENERATED:textmate-partial-reference
reference-partial.name: variable.other.reference.partial.lima

flow-sequence.comment: Inline sequence: [a, b, c]. A flow collection ends on its line (Core §7.4), so an unclosed `[` ends with the line.

flow-mapping.comment: Inline mapping: {key: val, key2: val2}. Ends on its line (Core §7.5), as a flow sequence does.

patterns.comment: A key and its separator, a colon followed by a space or a tab (Core 1.3 §7.5), and a comment right after it, which leaves the mapping unclosed. GENERATED:textmate-flow-mapping-key

quoted-string-double.comment: Lima Core §6.1.2. Only opens where no word character precedes the quote (\B), not mid-word — an unquoted value may contain a literal " or '. A string ends on its line. Valid escapes: \\ \" \/ \n \r \t \b \f \uXXXX \UXXXXXXXX \xXX; any other \x is unknown (strict: error; non-strict: left literal).
quoted-string-double.name: string.quoted.double.lima

quoted-string-single.comment: Lima Core §6.1.3. Only opens where no word character precedes the quote (\B) — otherwise an apostrophe in an unquoted value ("YAML's") would start a bogus string. A string ends on its line. Only special sequence is \' (an escaped quote); \\ is a two-character literal run.
quoted-string-single.name: string.quoted.single.lima

plain-word.comment: Words that hold no scalar although a part of one looks like it: joined by `-` (non-null, 10-20) or digits joined by two or more dots (1.2.3). No scope. GENERATED:textmate-plain-word

date.comment: Lima Core §6.5.1: ISO 8601 (with optional time and offset), plus German DD.MM.YYYY and slash DD/MM/YYYY forms. GENERATED:textmate-date
date.name: constant.other.date.lima
